candidates.original_title: Keeping one's distance: The influence of spatial distance cues on affect and evaluation
candidates.description: Plotting close-together points on graph paper causes people to report stronger emotional bonds to family and hometown compared to plotting distant points
candidates.citation_sentence: The first replication attempt focused on Study 4 of Williams and Bargh (2008), in which the 'spatial priming manipulation' was reported to have influenced people's feelings of emotional attachment to familiar people and places.
candidates.notes: Direct replication of Williams and Bargh (2008) Study 4. ANOVA showed no significant difference in bond strength between priming conditions, F(2,68)=.31, p=.73. Authors explicitly state neither study supported the original results. [ling26: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: Keeping one's distance: The influence of spatial distance cues on affect and evaluation
candidates.description: Physical-distance cues influence participants' estimates of the caloric content of unhealthy and healthy foods
candidates.citation_sentence: The second study attempted to replicate Study 3 of the same paper by Williams and Bargh (2008), which reported that physical-distance cues influenced participants' estimates of the caloric content of some 'unhealthy foods' such as french fries and ice cream, and some 'healthy foods' such as brown rice and apple.
candidates.notes: Direct replication of Williams and Bargh (2008) Study 3. No main effect of priming condition, F(2,85)=.53, p=.59; no significant interaction, F(2,85)=.45, p=.64. Authors state 'no support whatsoever for the findings of Williams and Bargh (2008).' [ling26: extra entry, not in the external record]
